alerts.title: Hypothyroidism uncontrolled with missed levothyroxine doses; weight gain may partly reflect thyroid dysfunction
alerts.message: Today's TSH is 12.4 mIU/L (target below 4.5) with low free T4, while patient reports weight gain of about 9 kg, fatigue, cold intolerance, constipation, dry skin and periorbital puffiness, consistent with under-replaced hypothyroidism. She often forgets her levothyroxine, which is a likely contributor. The guideline excerpts available here attribute abnormal weight gain to DTG as a listed adverse event, but the excerpts do not state that DTG causes weight gain, and the weight gain could be substantially driven by untreated hypothyroidism. Dose adequacy and adherence should be addressed before attributing the weight gain to DTG.

evidence.recommended_action: Address levothyroxine adherence (timing, reminders, pill organiser) and reassess thyroid function after an adequate interval before attributing weight gain to DTG. Consider levothyroxine dose review with the treating clinician.

alerts.title: Planned DTG switch for weight gain not supported by guideline evidence
alerts.message: The clinician proposes switching from DTG because of weight gain. The SAHCS guideline states DTG remains first-line for adults, including women of reproductive age, and that the association between integrase inhibitors and weight gain does not appear to be causal. Weight gain may instead reflect comparatively less metabolic toxicity of DTG versus older regimens. Given the untreated hypothyroidism and missed doses, a switch is premature.

evidence.recommended_action: Do not switch DTG on the basis of weight gain alone. Correct hypothyroidism and adherence first, then reassess weight and metabolic status before considering any regimen change.

alerts.title: Hyperglycaemia risk screening indicated: BMI ≥25 and age ≥30 on DTG
alerts.message: Patient is on DTG and has at least two hyperglycaemia risk factors (age 45, BMI 33), so the guideline flowchart directs glucose checking. Fasting glucose today is 5.6 mmol/L, which is below the diabetic range but warrants follow-up given the risk profile, and a family history of diabetes and hypertension status should be documented. Lipids are also elevated (total cholesterol 6.4, LDL 4.2, triglycerides 2.3 mmol/L).

evidence.recommended_action: Follow the DTG hyperglycaemia screening flowchart: document family history and blood pressure history, repeat glucose or HbA1c per protocol, and manage cardiovascular risk including lipids.

alerts.title: Viral load monitoring interval should be confirmed on DTG
alerts.message: Last viral load was <50 copies/mL on 2025-11-10, 106 days before today. The guideline recommends viral load every 6 months on DTG-based first-line ART, which would place the next check around May 2026. Adherence concerns (missed levothyroxine doses) also warrant confirming that adherence to ART itself is reliable.

evidence.recommended_action: Schedule the next viral load in line with the 6-monthly DTG monitoring interval and assess ART adherence at each visit.
